desc:
A garden is the straight line from position 0 to position n. There is a tap at every integer position 0, 1, ..., n. Tap i can be opened so that it waters the whole stretch from i - ranges[i] to i + ranges[i], inclusive (a range of 0 waters just one point). The stretch may extend beyond the garden.

Return the minimum number of taps that must be opened to water every point of [0, n], or -1 if it cannot be done.

n = 7, ranges = [1, 2, 1, 0, 2, 1, 0, 1]  ->  3

Taps 1 (waters -1 to 3), 4 (2 to 6) and 7 (6 to 8) cover everything. ranges has n + 1 entries.
hints: Every tap covers an interval [i - ranges[i], i + ranges[i]]. The task is now a minimum cover of [0, n] by intervals.
Process positions from left to right and remember, for every left end, the furthest right end of any interval starting there (clip left ends below 0 to 0).

Jump-game style: keep the current reach and the furthest reach seen so far. When you pass the current reach, open one more tap (jump to the furthest seen); if the furthest is not beyond the current reach you are stuck, return -1.
editorial: Convert each tap to the interval [max(0, i - r), min(n, i + r)] and store far[left] = max(far[left], right). The problem is exactly the minimum number of jumps in a jump game: from any position x you may use an interval starting at or before x to get to its right end, and the interval with the largest right end among those starting at or before the covered prefix is the best choice.

Scan x from 0 to n - 1, keeping cur_end (reach of the taps already opened), furthest (best reach among all intervals starting at or before x) and a counter. At x == cur_end you must open a tap: if furthest ≤ cur_end there is a gap, return -1; otherwise count it and set cur_end = furthest. Linear time and O(n) space; the greedy is correct for the same exchange reason as the interval-cover problem.
